November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

name: Retrocomputing Meets Modern Machine Intelligence (Free Giveaway!!)
description:

We will giveaway a modern-style retro computer board to a lucky attendee! :D

Thanks to our speakers Rich Lucente and Alex Jacocks!

### ***Retrocomputing Meets Modern Machine Intelligence***

*Explore how modern AI tooling breathes new life into classic architectures in this interactive, two-hour open-source workshop. Large language models help rapidly scaffold custom emulator cores and cross-compilers, disassemble vintage machine code, parse raster display quirks, and port 8-bit game logic across divergent architectures.*

*Following a short presentation, folks can have fun exploring a fleet of physical and hybrid systems. Explore BASIC and assembly language on an original TRS-80 Color Computer 2 running over modern networked storage via a FujiNet cartridge, run ultra-fast Z80 bare-metal builds on the Agon Light 2, and evaluate modern lightweight reimplementations on the Wildbits Jr2.*

\-\-\-

If you have any questions, or having trouble finding the place, reach out on the Tech Frederick discord ([https://discord.gg/YFKZ9dt66J](https://discord.gg/YFKZ9dt66J))!

name: WAUUG December
description:
The Washington Area Unity Users Group (WAUUG) is wrapping up the year together.
After restarting the group this fall, December is a chance to celebrate the people who showed up, the projects everyone has been working on, the connections we’ve made, and the community we’re beginning to rebuild across DC, Maryland, and Northern Virginia.
This will be a relaxed end-of-year meetup for Unity developers, game developers, artists, designers, students, hobbyists, industry professionals, and anyone interested in creating games or interactive experiences.
Come hang out, talk games, share what you’ve been building, meet other developers, and reflect on what you worked on in 2026. Finished something this year? Bring it. Still working on something? Bring that too. Have nothing to show yet but want to meet people and get inspired for next year? You’re just as welcome.
This meetup is also an opportunity to talk about where WAUUG goes next. We want 2027 to include more opportunities for community members to present projects, teach what they know, participate in workshops and game jams, collaborate with others, and connect with developers throughout the region.
You do **not** need to be a Unity expert. Beginners, students, indie developers, professional developers, artists, designers, and curious newcomers are all welcome.

**Thursday, December 17, 2026**
**6:30–8:30 PM**
**Ocelot Brewing Company — Dulles, VA**

Great people create amazing things. Come share what you’re building, talk games, celebrate the community, and help us close out WAUUG’s restart year on a high note.

name: W36 CSTGIA 2026: Agentic Trust
description:
### CSTGIA 2026 — Week 36

From Cyber Response Advantage to Agentic Trust
When AI Can Act, Trust Must Become Executable

AI is moving from answering questions to taking action.
Agents can increasingly access systems, invoke tools, communicate with other agents, execute workflows, modify environments, and act on behalf of people and organizations.

That changes the cybersecurity question. It is no longer simply: “Can we trust the AI?” It becomes: “Can we trust what the AI is authorized to do?”

In Week 36, Dr. Rhonda Farrell explores Agentic Trust and the emerging Autonomous Authority Gap. We examine agent identity, dynamic authority, behavioral monitoring, runtime governance, human-agent accountability, and the evolution of Zero Trust from securing access toward securing agency.

The episode also includes a practical 15-Minute Agent Authority Test leaders can use to examine one AI agent across identity, ownership, purpose, data, tools, permissions, actions, and escalation.
Know the Agent. Bound the Authority. Verify the Action. Preserve the Accountability.

🎥 **Watch on YouTube:** https://youtu.be/tViwU9J3IY8

🔔 Subscribe for the next CSTGIA 2026 conversation on the technologies, risks, workforce capabilities, and leadership decisions shaping the future of cybersecurity.

🔔 New episodes of CSTGIA 2026 are released weekly, exploring the emerging trends, technologies, leadership strategies, and enterprise capabilities shaping the future of cybersecurity and organizational excellence.

#CSTGIA #Cybersecurity #AgenticAI #AgenticSecurity #DigitalTrust #ZeroTrust #IdentitySecurity #AIGovernance #CyberLeadership #CyberResilience #MachineIdentity #ArtificialIntelligence

name: Special Speaking Event: Vegan Climate Healers
description:
Earthsave is proud and privileged to present the internationally celebrated environmental advocate **Dr. Sailesh Rao**, Founder and Executive Director of Climate Healers. After earning a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from Stanford University, he spent two decades working on internet communications infrastructure and protocol design, earning prestigious professional accolades along the way. His pioneering efforts helped move computer technology into the digital age. In 2006, he pivoted to full-time environmental advocacy.

Dr. Rao has authored several books, numerous peer-reviewed technical papers, and served as an Executive Producer on major documentaries such as ***Cowspiracy***, ***What The Health***, and ***The End of Medicine***. He was named a Climate Hero by The Guardian Newspaper in 2023. Join us for a fascinating presentation by Dr. Rao about creating a climate-healing food system.

Admission is $15 for those who bring a vegan snack or dessert, and $20 for those who attend without bringing food. Attendees pay at the door. Fees will help sustain the work of the Earthsave Baltimore nonprofit group and the Baltimore Veg/Vegan Meetup group. Please RSVP at [https://www.meetup.com/the-baltimore-vegan-meetup-group/](https://www.meetup.com/the-baltimore-vegan-meetup-group/) Hope to see you there!

name: Science, Technology & Sci-Fi - Pennsylvania
description:
We're based in south central Pennsylvania. At this time we're mostly meeting online, but some of us who live near each other get together in person. For our next online Meetup on the fourth Wednesday of the month, 7:00 pm - 8:30 pm, you can participate either by webcam or telephone call. The link will be sent by early evening to everyone who has RSVPd, and we will check for late RSVPs by 6:00 pm that day.

We recommend that you RSVP from the Events page:
https://www.meetup.com/sci-fi-and-sci/

It's best to RSVP early, because once we start the Meetup at 7:00 pm that day, we might not notice any late RSVPs.

You can participate either by webcam or telephone call. We will send a link that day around 5:30 or 6:00 pm to everyone who RSVPd, and will check for late RSVPs by 6:30 pm that day.

If you don't see the link in your Inbox by 6:00 pm that day, check your spam folder, or send a note directly to the organizer https://www.meetup.com/sci-and-sci-fi/members/?op=leaders

Feel free to bring up any aspect of science & society, or science fiction. Topics can include either: (a) natural sciences, social sciences, philosophy, philosophy of science, technology, industry, science & society; or (b) science fiction (movies, novels, TV shows, etc. Also, you might have suggestions for some upcoming group activities, such as going to a movie, museum, or other event, as a group. New members might want to tell a bit about their interests.

name: Maryland Blockchain Association & CryptoMondays Virtual Meetup
description:
Network virtually with those located in the DMV (District of Columbia, Virginia & Maryland) and internationally!

This monthly Monday meeting is hosted by Maryland Blockchain Association, Blockchain Legal Institute, and Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is the Maryland Chapter Lead for CryptoMondays. The MDBA's monthly virtual networking event is hosted monthly on the 1st Monday of each month. If you are interested in establishing a meetup in alliance with the MDBA and CryptoMondays please reach out.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is a trade association dedicated to representing the innovative tech community within Maryland to provide education, economic development and outreach to those within our local community.

CryptoMondays is a decentralized global community that brings together individuals passionate about cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.

The Blockchain Legal Institute is a centralized library of decentralized resources & the only Institute specifically dedicated to help provide continuing education to lawyers, compliance officers, business professionals and those learning about digital assets.

The Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation is a non profit dedicated to developing digital asset educational resources for consumers and families.

Learn about the latest trends in digital currency and blockchain technology, and gain insights into the world of crypto-tokens, Bitcoin, Ethereum as well as updates involving the regulations impacting consumers and businesses within our world of blockchain, IoT, RWA, artificial intelligence, and innovative technology. Expert speakers will cover blockchain security, cryptography, and other relevant topics in the fast-evolving cryptocurrency market.

Whether you are a seasoned investor or new to the world of virtual currency, these virtual events are the perfect opportunity to network locally and internationally with like-minded individuals and expand your knowledge in the realm of enterprise blockchain technology.

Don't miss out on this chance to stay ahead of the curve and explore the exciting opportunities that cryptocurrency and blockchain technology have to offer.

[www.bli.tools](www.bli.tools)
[www.marylandblockchainassociation.org](www.marylandblockchainassociation.org)
[www.bli.foundation](www.bli.foundation)
[cryptomondays.io](http://cryptomondays.io/ "http://cryptomondays.io")

Mark Your Calendars for the 1st Monday of every Month! This event is hosted on a private zoom link to be shared after registration.

Speakers: Jacqueline Cooper, JD & Other Special Guests

Be sure to mark your calendar as we have speakers from around the globe to attend our Meet-Ups. Speakers will include those with knowledge about artificial intelligence, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tokens, Blockchain use cases, compliance, business development, DeFi, estate planning, finance, accounting, and so many other relevant topics.

Jacqueline Cooper, JD, NBCT, MA LDT, CCI, BMM: CEO: Blockchain Legal Institute, Founder: Maryland Blockchain Association, Partner of Cogent Law Group, Government Blockchain Association: Co-Chair Legal Working Group & GBA Talk Show Host, Global Blockchain Business Council, Media Ambassador, Author: Bitcoin Cinderella Blockchain Adventure series, Author: The Essential Digital Asset Organizer for Attorneys & Their Clients, Author: How to Use Digital Assets To Fundraise For Your Non Profit

name: threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing
description:
Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

name: PLUG Central - Jitsi Meet: 7-9PM; Speaker from 7:30-8:30PM
description:
Please join us for PLUG Central. During the pandemic we meet on-line at Jitsi Meet, beginning at 7pm. RSVPs are optional. Anyone interested in Linux and Free and Open Source software is welcome to attend. We welcome all levels of expertise, whether you're just curious, a hobbyist, or a professional.

Jitsi Meet agenda:

Q&A with emcee CJ Fearnley from 7-7:30PM. Bring your Linux (and related) questions for a group exploration.

The main presentation from 7:30-8:30PM: TBD.

Q&A continued from 8:30-9PM.

After the pandemic dissipates, we plan to again meet in Lecture Hall A in Griffith Hall at USP in Philadelphia. We plan to revert to the original speaker slot from 8-9PM with Q&A at the beginning to better support travel constraints.

After the presentation some of us adjourn to Clarkville (http://www.clarkvillephilly.com/) a nearby pizza and craft beer restaurant.

University of the Sciences in Philadelphia (USP)
Griffith Hall (Room "A" or "C", look for the signs)
600 South 43rd Street
Philadelphia, PA 19104-4495

USP is located in University City. Driving directions are available at http://www.phillylinux.org/locations/usp.html, or http://www.usip.edu/directions, both of which have an aerial view of the campus buildings. USP is also easily accessible by public transportation.

Often, the door to Griffith Hall is locked at 7PM. If you find the door locked, please contact the security guard (usually in the booth in the parking lot) and tell them that the monthly PLUG (Philadelphia Linux User Group) meeting in Griffith Hall is tonight. If there is no one in the booth you can call UCS's public safety number at 215.895.1117 and they will radio personnel to unlock the door. Our sponsor is Zhiwei Liu in the Chemistry department. Security knows this and will almost always open the door for you and have it unlocked so other participants can enter without issue.

name: Micah Johnson: "Aku: Battle For Pyra"
description:
Aku, space traveler of the metaverse, is BACK and ready to blast off in book two of this action-packed sci-fi series, where he and his friends must travel to a fiery planet to recover a gem of untold power, lest it fall into the wrong hands. 

 

After saving the planet Ibra from a ruthless space militia, Aku is ready for a break. But when his grandfather announces an urgent mission to the fiery, lava-filled planet Pyra, Aku and his friends end up on their most dangerous mission yet.

 

What awaits them is a world forged in lava and legend. Here, ancient beings guard the GEM: a radiant core said to control the light of the universe. To claim the GEM, Aku’s crew must survive three deadly trials—racing through molten mazes, battling in a gravity-defying magmaball arena, and descending into the planet’s core itself—before Aku comes face-to-face with his greatest enemy…and the truth about his family’s past.

 

Filled with humor and high-octane twists, this is a cosmic coming-of-age story about courage, legacy, and the value of finding your winning team.

 

 

About the Author:

 

Micah Johnson is a former Major League Baseball player turned artist, is the creator of the phenomenon that is Aku, a 3D animated boy wearing an oversized astronaut helmet. Micah’s fine art piece catapulted him from retired athlete to creator of the 2020 NFT of the Year. Aku: Journey to Ibra is Aku’s origin story and Micah’s first book. He lives in Maine with his wife and daughters.

 

About the Program:

 

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 3 pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last. Free street parking and bike parking are available.

threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing
description:
Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

CONVERGE helps startups bring biomanufacturing technologies developed at Aberdeen Proving Ground (APG) to market and trains the workforce that will power them, which makes it the right place to start this conversation. The evening will focus on the breakthrough work coming out of APG, the unique challenges defense-sector companies face, where the region's biggest opportunities lie, and how our entrepreneurial ecosystem can step up to support the companies working in this space. You'll be in the room with innovators, technologists, workforce development experts, elected officials, Department of War officials, and the anchor institutions shaping the region's defense and national security future. Together, we'll build the partnerships and shared commitment that will position the Greater Baltimore Region to lead in this field. Register and mark your calendar now. The full program, speaker lineup, and additional details will be announced in the coming months. Stay tuned. You won't want to miss this one.

November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

name: Embassy of Zimbabwe Reception
description:
To secure your spot, purchase your ticket from the Eventbrite link ([https://www.eventbrite.com/e/embassy-of-zimbabwe-reception-safari-and-beyond-tickets-2001255937381](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/embassy-of-zimbabwe-reception-safari-and-beyond-tickets-2001255937381)). RSVPing only on the Meetup Page doesn't allow you to attend the Event. ADVANCE TICKET PURCHASE IS REQUIRED.

ABOUT THE EVENT

You are cordially invited to join us at the Embassy of Zimbabwe for a night filled with fun and information on the country's culture, economy, business and mainly tourism.
Witness the majesty of wildlife roaming free in the National Parks, feel the spray of the mighty Victoria Falls and experience the warmth of Zimbabweans whose hospitality shines with genuine joy, and no visit is complete without indulging in Zimbabwe’s rich **gastronomy**.

Zimbabwe has several major tourist attractions. Victoria Falls on the Zambezi river is one of them. It is considered to be the largest waterfall in the world.
The Victoria Falls National Park is also in this area and is one of the eight main national parks in the country. The largest of which is Hwange National Park. Lake Kariba another site for tourism, is the largest reservoir in the world.

Zimbabwe is unusual in Africa in that there are a number of ancient and medieval ruined cities built in a unique dry stone style. Among the most famous of these are the Great Zimbabwe ruins in Masvingo.

Zimbabwe is also the third largest producer of platinum and one of the largest producers of gold.

For Google Chrome Users :

Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

name: Tiffany Hammond: "How Do You Spell Belong?"
description:
Rainy days are perfect for museum visits, and Aidan is excited to learn. But with the umbrella weather comes long lines and loud sounds. As with others with Autism, these sensations overwhelm Aidan. His brain gets fuzzy and his eyes get blurry, and he grunts, shouts, and slaps his chest to express his feelings.

 

Some people don't know why Aidan reacts this way. Rather than trying to understand him, they stare at him strangely and whisper, making him feel like he doesn't belong, that he should leave. But just because Aidan communicates in different ways, doesn't mean he should hide himself.

 

Then another child reaches out, not with judgment but with curiosity. She invites Aidan to explore the exhibits with her, and this one act of kindness makes a world of difference. With the help of his dad and his new friend, Aidan is able to be himself, proving to others and to himself that he belongs.

 

From the bestselling author and creator of the "Fidgets and Fries"  platform comes a touching, engaging picture book that encourages us all to create a more inclusive, welcoming world.

 

 

About the Author:

Tiffany Hammond is the voice behind the popular social media platform, "Fidgets and Fries." She is an autistic storyteller from Texas who raises two children with autism diagnoses as well. Through stories, poems, and essays, she challenges the perception of autism as a lifelong sentence of doom and gloom, inspires thought leaders, and cultivates a community that explores the concept of Intersectionality. She is a speaker, consultant, and advocate for all. Her debut picture book, A Day with No Words was an instant #1 NYT bestseller. You can visit her at her website  at www.tiffanyhammond.com

 

 

About the Program:

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 3pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last. Bike parking and metered street parking are available.

name: Find a Startup to Help or Join
description:
**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

name: Booklovers' Breakfast featuring Deesha Philyaw
description:
We’re honored to welcome award-winning author Deesha Philyaw as the speaker for this year’s Booklovers' Breakfast on Saturday, February 6, 2027, 8:30am - noon, at the Baltimore Marriott Waterfront (700 Aliceanna Street, Baltimore, MD 21202). 

 

Deesha Philyaw is the author of the debut novel, The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman. Her debut short story collection, The Secret Lives of Church Ladies, won the PEN/Faulkner Award for Fiction, the Story Prize, the LA Times Book Prize: The Art Seidenbaum Award for First Fiction and was a finalist for the National Book Award for Fiction. Deesha is a Kimbilio Fiction Fellow, a Baldwin for the Arts Fellow, a United States Artists Fellow, and co-host of two podcasts, Ursa Short Fiction (with Dawnie Walton) and Reckon True Stories (with Kiese Laymon). She is currently at work developing TV shows based on her short fiction.

 

The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman (Mariner Books, September 29, 2025) tells the story of the wife of a popular and powerful megachurch pastor whose charmed “rags-to-Rolex” life is upended when her secret past comes roaring into the spotlight.

name: Grand-Parenting 101
description:
Contact Name: Amy Brown
Contact Email: Childbirthed@umm.edu
Department: Women's Center
Category: Childbirth
Link: https://www.umms.org/ummc/health-services/womens-health/obstetrics-gynecology/pregnancy-childbirth/classes

**This class is VIRTUAL**

Added by popular demand, this two-hour class covers the infant care and infant CPR basics that grandparents need to know.  This class is one part newborn refresher course and one part education about how that care has changed since you were raising kids.  Topics covered include:
  • Appearance, senses, crying and communication
  • Soothing and sleeping
  • Feeding
  • Newborn care tips, including diapering and bathing
  • Infant CPR, including how to handle choking
  • Car seat and travel safety

name: threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing
description:
Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

description:
Location: This is a hybrid meeting. RSVP for the meeting link or in-person location

  • To join in person: Meet us at 6:30pm to get to know the team over vegetarian dinner
  • To join virtually: Join our google meet room at 7:00pm for hybrid updates on our campaign priorities and small group actions. 

Who we are:

District of Columbia—Climate Action Network (DC-CAN) is a DC-based action team of volunteers who support Chesapeake Climate Action Network (CCAN) climate justice and clean energy campaigns. We also launch our own climate-related actions.

Mission Statement: 

Our purpose is to work together to improve the health and legacy of Washington DC communities—human and nonhuman alike—by undertaking local campaigns that reverse or prevent climate change and the inequity arising from it. We welcome those who want to organize and build power to address the climate crisis, to live more harmoniously with the environment, and to pass on a liveable planet to generations to come.

About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

Topics can include either: (a) natural sciences, social sciences, philosophy, philosophy of science, technology, industry, science & society; or (b) science fiction (movies, novels, TV shows, etc. Also, you might have suggestions for some upcoming group activities, such as going to a movie, museum, or other event, as a group. name: CA Board of Directors Meeting
Find a Startup to Help or Join
description:
**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

name: Kate Messner: "Keep the Ghost Light On"
description:
A haunted Broadway theater.
A ghost demanding justice.
Three kids who must follow the clues to unlock the past . . .

 

When Daphne, Luna, and Felix break into a shuttered theater to produce their own musical, they find it haunted by the ghost of an angry showgirl who makes a cryptic demand:

 

TRUTH

 

Daphne is already struggling with her own truth, ever since a cute older boy humiliated her in front of the drama club last spring. Now her heart is full of secrets, and she hasn't written a new song in months.

 

But the ghost is persistent, and the friends find themselves sleuthing through empty research libraries and abandoned theaters in a search for answers. As the hauntings escalate from spooky to deadly, can they uncover the truth of what happened a century ago and finally free their ghosts?

 

Told via stage play, song lyrics, letters, and more this fast-paced, accessible novel will capture any reader.

 

About the Author:

Kate Messner is a former middle-school English teacher and the author of E. B. White Read Aloud Award winner The Brilliant Fall of Gianna Z. and its companion, The Exact Location of Home; Sugar and Ice; Eye of the Storm; Wake Up Missing; All the Answers; The Seventh Wish; Capture the Flag; Hide and Seek; the Marty McGuire chapter book series; the Ranger in Time chapter book series; and several picture books. She lives on Lake Champlain with her husband and two kids. When she’s not reading or writing, she loves hiking, kayaking, biking, and watching thunderstorms over the lake. Visit her website at www.katemessner.com.

 

About the Program:

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 2pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last. Free street parking is available along the side of the building.

name: Maryland Blockchain Association & CryptoMondays Virtual Meetup
description:
Network virtually with those located in the DMV (District of Columbia, Virginia & Maryland) and internationally!

This monthly Monday meeting is hosted by Maryland Blockchain Association, Blockchain Legal Institute, and Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is the Maryland Chapter Lead for CryptoMondays. The MDBA's monthly virtual networking event is hosted monthly on the 1st Monday of each month. If you are interested in establishing a meetup in alliance with the MDBA and CryptoMondays please reach out.

The Maryland Blockchain Association is a trade association dedicated to representing the innovative tech community within Maryland to provide education, economic development and outreach to those within our local community.

CryptoMondays is a decentralized global community that brings together individuals passionate about cryptocurrency and blockchain technology.

The Blockchain Legal Institute is a centralized library of decentralized resources & the only Institute specifically dedicated to help provide continuing education to lawyers, compliance officers, business professionals and those learning about digital assets.

The Blockchain Legal Institute Foundation is a non profit dedicated to developing digital asset educational resources for consumers and families.

Learn about the latest trends in digital currency and blockchain technology, and gain insights into the world of crypto-tokens, Bitcoin, Ethereum as well as updates involving the regulations impacting consumers and businesses within our world of blockchain, IoT, RWA, artificial intelligence, and innovative technology. Expert speakers will cover blockchain security, cryptography, and other relevant topics in the fast-evolving cryptocurrency market.

Whether you are a seasoned investor or new to the world of virtual currency, these virtual events are the perfect opportunity to network locally and internationally with like-minded individuals and expand your knowledge in the realm of enterprise blockchain technology.

Don't miss out on this chance to stay ahead of the curve and explore the exciting opportunities that cryptocurrency and blockchain technology have to offer.

[www.bli.tools](www.bli.tools)
[www.marylandblockchainassociation.org](www.marylandblockchainassociation.org)
[www.bli.foundation](www.bli.foundation)
[cryptomondays.io](http://cryptomondays.io/ "http://cryptomondays.io")

Mark Your Calendars for the 1st Monday of every Month! This event is hosted on a private zoom link to be shared after registration.

Speakers: Jacqueline Cooper, JD & Other Special Guests

Be sure to mark your calendar as we have speakers from around the globe to attend our Meet-Ups. Speakers will include those with knowledge about artificial intelligence, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tokens, Blockchain use cases, compliance, business development, DeFi, estate planning, finance, accounting, and so many other relevant topics.

Jacqueline Cooper, JD, NBCT, MA LDT, CCI, BMM: CEO: Blockchain Legal Institute, Founder: Maryland Blockchain Association, Partner of Cogent Law Group, Government Blockchain Association: Co-Chair Legal Working Group & GBA Talk Show Host, Global Blockchain Business Council, Media Ambassador, Author: Bitcoin Cinderella Blockchain Adventure series, Author: The Essential Digital Asset Organizer for Attorneys & Their Clients, Author: How to Use Digital Assets To Fundraise For Your Non Profit

name: James Riley: "The Dragon's Apprentice"
description:
The first book of a hilarious fantasy adventure series from the author of Story Thieves, a girl strikes a deal with the ancient, cranky dragon she accidentally summoned to teach her the forbidden magic she needs to save her mother.

 

STOP. Don’t read any further. There are magic spells in this book, and the Emperor has forbidden anyone from learning magic, because it’s way too dangerous! If you try one of the spells, any number of terrible things might happen (or so the Emperor says).

 

Don’t be like Ciara, a twelve-year-old girl living in the tiny village of Skael. When she used a spell from within this book, she ended up summoning a dragon. A DRAGON! Those things breathe fire! From their mouths! She’s obviously doomed.

 

And don’t listen if Ciara tells you that dragons won’t hurt humans, and that they even once taught us magic, a thousand years ago. Definitely don’t pay any attention to the fact that the dragon she summoned, Scorch, might be willing to help rescue Ciara’s mother and free her village from the Emperor and his Warden, because it’s all obviously a big lie. So put this book down, and forget about it. Magic is just way too dangerous. After all, you wouldn’t want to summon your own dragon, would you?

 

About the Author:

James Riley is the New York Times bestselling author of the Story Thieves, Half Upon a Time, Once Upon Another Time, Revenge of Magic, and the Dragon's Apprentice series. He’s never apprenticed with a dragon . . . yet. He’s pretty sure there’s still time, though, especially if he could do it as an online video apprenticeship sort of thing. Does that exist? If not, it should: Learn Magic over Zoom (and Try Not to Burn Down Your House)!

 

About the Program:

To attend in person please register here. Doors will open to registered attendees at 3pm. All registered in person attendees will receive a free copy of the book while supplies last. Free street parking is available along the side of the building.

name: threadHOURS® at TouchPoint - Ongoing
description:
Every Wednesday | 3-6 pm
Location:
TouchPoint: 3201 Tioga Parkway, Suite P, Baltimore, MD 21215
About:
Join us each Wednesday to strengthen relationships and explore post-high school pathways. Get in-person Thread Family planning & support.
Who should attend?
Open to all Thread young people and volunteers looking for programming, resources, activities, and partners to support post high school pathways and plans.
How do I support?
You can RSVP in advance using the links below, or just show up (bring other volunteers and young people with you!) If you like having a specific role you can sign ahead of time
here
, or just ask for a role when you get to the check-in table!!!
November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

November Focus: Check In, Stay Connected, Keep Moving Forward!
November is here, and our post-high-school young people are settling into
new jobs, college classes, training programs, and Maryland Corps / Service Year placements!
With the excitement of new beginnings behind us, now is the time to check in, see how things are really going, and make sure young people have the support they need to keep moving forward.
Each Wednesday at TouchPoint
threadHOURS
, young people can connect with staff, volunteers, and resource partners to troubleshoot challenges, access resources, and take their next steps. Whether they're struggling with a new placement, navigating college or work, facing financial pressures, or figuring out what's next, threadHOURS is a place to get support and keep building momentum.
As
Maryland Corps / Service Year applications wrap up
, our focus is shifting from getting young people into opportunities to
helping them succeed once they're there!
And with the holiday season approaching, it's an especially important time to stay connected, celebrate progress, and catch challenges before they become bigger barriers.
How you can roll as a volunteer:
This month, make the check-in count!
Reach out to your young person and ask how things are
really
going. Are they feeling good about school, work, or Service Year? What's going well? What's getting in the way? Are there any concerns or needs that might become more pressing as the holidays approach?
Don't just check the box — help connect the dots!
Celebrate their wins, listen for challenges, and make sure any concerns get elevated to Thread staff so we can help address them. Better yet, come to threadHOURS together and turn those conversations into action.
Your consistency, encouragement, and follow-through can make all the difference!

  • To join in person: Meet us at 6:30pm to get to know the team over vegetarian dinner
  • To join virtually: Join our google meet room at 7:00pm for hybrid updates on our campaign priorities and small group actions. 

Who we are:

District of Columbia—Climate Action Network (DC-CAN) is a DC-based action team of volunteers who support Chesapeake Climate Action Network (CCAN) climate justice and clean energy campaigns. We also launch our own climate-related actions.

Mission Statement: 

Our purpose is to work together to improve the health and legacy of Washington DC communities—human and nonhuman alike—by undertaking local campaigns that reverse or prevent climate change and the inequity arising from it. We welcome those who want to organize and build power to address the climate crisis, to live more harmoniously with the environment, and to pass on a liveable planet to generations to come.

description:
Try an ollie; take to the air. Jump and land; show off your flair. This rhythmic ode to skateboarding revealed through vivid graphic art beckons readers to hop on and spin round and round, cause you're sure to be Olympics bound! 

 

About the Author:

Carole Boston Weatherford is a New York Times bestselling author of 60-plus books including the Caldecott Honor book Unspeakable: The Tulsa Race Massacre, for which she was also awarded the Coretta Scott King Author Award and a Sibert Honor; the Newbery Honor winner Box; and the Caldecott Honor winners Freedom in Congo Square, Fannie Lou Hamer, and Moses. She won a Coretta Scott King Author Honor for Becoming Billie Holiday. Weatherford teaches composition and children's literature at Fayetteville State University in North Carolina. Visit cbweatherford.com.

name: CA Board of Directors Meeting
Find a Startup to Help or Join
description:
**Welcome!**

The official registration page is [here](Startupoasisvirtual.eventbrite.com).

If you are a developer, UX designer, marketer, or anyone else in the tech ecosystem looking to join or help a tech startup, or even just get involved in a project, this event is for you!

We will be introducing projects for you to get involved with during the pitches. There is no group like this on Meetup or in the startup world because we filter out the BS and get you going on a project ASAP.

(Stay inside the Startup Oasis by joining our [newsletter](https://mailchi.mp/startupoasis/meetup)!)

What happens first in the event is startup founders pitch their business or idea to the audience, which is full of the developers, designers, marketers, etc.

If you are interested in one of the projects / startups, you can join one of the founders in a breakout room to continue building, workshopping, and/or onboarding the startup with attendees.

People have been able to start and advance their businesses as a result of this process.

We are meeting on Zoom, the link is here in the listing.

**Agenda:**
**Intros:** During the first 10 minutes, we will give you the history, structure, and future plans of Startup Oasis and open signups for founders that want to pitch their startups.

**Pitches:** Each founder will then get up to 3 minutes to pitch their startup. This format is recommended: name, business, the problem, your solution, target customer base, and your biggest challenge/current need. This part is similar to Shark Tank.

**Breakout Groups:** For the remainder of the event, each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk to the founders in greater detail about their needs and challenges in a small group setting. This part is similar to a hackathon.

Startup Oasis was created to pierce the illusion of accessibility of startups and tech by creating a grassroots forum for early-stage founders to pitch to those in the tech ecosystem to get real-time feedback for their idea or business.

Use this [link](https://lnk.bio/startup.oasis) to:

* Follow us on LinkedIn
* Join our community on Discord
* Donate to our cause
* Visit our website

**FAQ:**
**Is this event free to attend?** Yes - Startup Oasis will always be free for anyone to attend. If you would like to donate, you can do so directly on our [website](https://donate.stripe.com/eVa2a0dV27Nlb2ofYY). You can also talk to us about volunteer or sponsorship opportunities.

**How do I sign up to pitch?** RSVP here. Right when the event starts, fill out the form and then raise your hand on Zoom. That will also determine the order. You can also buy a VIP ticket to support our cause and guarantee you a spot to pitch. To be eligible to pitch, you must be the cofounder of a technology-based startup. Agencies, consultants, coaches, MLM schemes, and nonprofits are not eligible to pitch, but you can still watch the pitches and join the breakouts.

**What happens after the pitches?** The breakout groups open for the remainder of the event. Each founder gets a breakout room, and you can talk more about their business and needs with them.

**Can I invite other people that I know?** Yes - please have them RSVP here or on the [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/startup-oasis-global) event listing.

**How do I get the most out of this event?**

* Founders - In this event, no money is awarded nor are any winners named. We are not here to critique your pitch, just to help you find teammates, cofounders, and feedback from other professionals. Make sure your pitch is 3 minutes or less and clear about what your biggest needs are.
* Attendees - If you are new to startups and tech, feel free to just watch with no pressure to participate. If you are looking to join a startup or find a side project, make sure you take notes during the pitches to join the group of the founder that you're most interested in helping. Most founders need help with either developing the product or with a go-to-market strategy.
*

**Do we meet in person?** We do this event in Atlanta, GA each month in Midtown at ATDC.

**Content:** We are looking for founders to be interviewed or people to interview founders for short videos. Let us know if you are interested!

Who we are:

District of Columbia—Climate Action Network (DC-CAN) is a DC-based action team of volunteers who support Chesapeake Climate Action Network (CCAN) climate justice and clean energy campaigns. We also launch our own climate-related actions.

Mission Statement: 

Our purpose is to work together to improve the health and legacy of Washington DC communities—human and nonhuman alike—by undertaking local campaigns that reverse or prevent climate change and the inequity arising from it. We welcome those who want to organize and build power to address the climate crisis, to live more harmoniously with the environment, and to pass on a liveable planet to generations to come.

description:
Hosted by the Alliance for the Chesapeake Bay and Penn State Extension, the
So You Want To Grow…
Webinar Series is for anyone who wants to learn how to grow native trees and shrubs.
Topics to Be Covered
Each webinar will highlight different native tree or shrub species and include technical information on methods for germinating seeds and growing seedlings for conservation projects or your own backyard! Attendees will learn how to identify native trees and shrubs, their ecology, when and how to harvest their seeds for propagation, and the benefits that these plants provide to the ecosystem.
You don’t need to be a seasoned grower or have a greenhouse to grow native trees and shrubs!
This webinar series is free to attend. Please register using the links below.

The DEF CON Group 443, also known as DC443, is an interest group designed to discuss general hacking and its culture, information security (InfoSec), and related topics. name: DC-CAN Monthly Meeting [Hybrid Event: In-person and Virtual Options]
description:
Location: This is a hybrid meeting. RSVP for the meeting link or in-person location

  • To join in person: Meet us at 6:30pm to get to know the team over vegetarian dinner
  • To join virtually: Join our google meet room at 7:00pm for hybrid updates on our campaign priorities and small group actions. 

Who we are:

District of Columbia—Climate Action Network (DC-CAN) is a DC-based action team of volunteers who support Chesapeake Climate Action Network (CCAN) climate justice and clean energy campaigns. We also launch our own climate-related actions.

Mission Statement: 

Our purpose is to work together to improve the health and legacy of Washington DC communities—human and nonhuman alike—by undertaking local campaigns that reverse or prevent climate change and the inequity arising from it. We welcome those who want to organize and build power to address the climate crisis, to live more harmoniously with the environment, and to pass on a liveable planet to generations to come.

description:
SUMMARY:
The DEF CON Group 443, also known as DC443, is an interest group designed to discuss general hacking and its culture, information security (InfoSec), and related topics. Our group’s interests include InfoSec, SDR, Hackathons, Speaker Events (MiniCons), Capture The Flags (CTFs), Binary Reversing/Exploitation, Ham Radio, Lock Picking, Micro Electronics, Web Development, etc.

We plan to meet every other week on Fridays at Unallocated space. Meetings can include Talks, projects, trivia nights, workshops, or contests and CTFs.

Website: https://dc443.org
Twitter: https://twitter.com/dc443_

GOAL: Learn about new and existing interests and grow the Unallocated Space community.

THINGS TO BRING: Yourself and friends

SKILL LEVEL:
Any

description:
Monday evenings, we will be open for Project Night - a night to work on, collaborate on, or brainstorm on whatever projects you're currently working on or interested in.

name: DECEMBER - VC in DC's Third Thursdays
A Night At The Embassy of The European Union
description:
To secure your spot, purchase your ticket from the link ([https://www.eventbrite.com/e/a-night-at-the-european-union-embassydelegation-tickets-544451849137](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/a-night-at-the-european-union-embassydelegation-tickets-544451849137)). RSVPing only on the Meetup Page doesn't allow you to attend the Event. ADVANCE TICKET PURCHASE IS REQUIRED.

ABOUT THE EVENT

You are cordially invited to step on to the soil of the European Union, for a night filled with fun and information, on European culture, economy, business and tourism.

We meet, greet, network and socialize with European diplomats throughout the evening. Diplomats will deliver speeches on how the youth in Europe became environment conscious and what we could learn from that, here in the states.

RUNDOWN :

1. **BUFFET** : European finger food will be served.
2. **OPEN BAR** : European drinks, all night long.
3. **DRESS CODE** : Business/Cocktail.
4. **FORMAT** : This is primarily a stand up, buffet style reception, throughout the evening. However, a limited number of chairs will be around.
5. **TICKETS AVAILABILITY** : Very limited. Grab yours before we sell out. Also, prices are subject to increases as inventory declines.

**Payment Instructions :**

1\. You should login from a PC to see the 'Pay Now' button\, after RSVPing\. Then hit the button\.
2\. Verify correct dollar amount for number of people you're paying for\.
**3\. If you don't have a Paypal account\, click "Pay with a Debit or Credit Card"\.**
4\. If you have a Paypal account\, simply log in\, and pay as you normally would via Paypal\.

***How to Unblock the Pop-up Blocker on Your Phone***

Many of our patrons advised us that they have a Pop-up Blocker on their iPhones and it hinders them from buying tickets. To unblock, please follow the following steps :

For Safari Users :
1\. Go to Settings\.
2\. Scroll down to Safari and click on it\.
3\. Select Block Pop\-ups and turn it off\.

For Google Chrome Users :
1\. Open Google Chrome\.
2\. Click on the three dots and you will see many options\.
3\. Click on Settings\.
4\. Scroll down to content settings\.
5\. Select Block Pop\-ups and turn it off\.
